title: Go code people write
description: How the Go code of STEGO that people write by hand is accounted for, under the code standard ST-STD-CODE. No tooling record of STEGO generates STEGO's own code, and nothing outside STEGO provides it. Thus each technical record is a fill at one of three slots: the logic, the storage shape or the wiring that a person writes. The count of fills at each slot is the backlog of what a person writes. What STEGO can one day derive from its own specification is in the storage shape and the wiring slots.
notes: Decided by the Product owner on 2026-11-04: the hand-written technical records are fills, grouped by what a person writes, so that the count per slot is honest. Every domain follows the pattern itself, so it has no settings. The engineering standards and their rules are accidental too, but Lathe has no fill for a standard, so they are not at a slot.

title: Tests that run locally
description: How a domain's tests are run, under the quality standard ST-STD-LOCAL: on a developer's workstation, from one command per suite, with local stand-ins for outside systems, with local services that the suite starts at pinned versions, and with no state left outside a temporary folder. A shared cluster or a hosted service gives a second proof only.
notes: Decided by the Product owner on 2026-11-05. Lathe lets a domain follow a pattern, not a standard, so this pattern carries the standard into each domain, as ST-PAT-GO-CODE carries ST-STD-CODE. Each rule of the pattern holds one rule of ST-STD-LOCAL for the tests of one domain, so Lathe asks for one test per rule and domain. The pattern has no settings: each domain follows it as it is.
